t: A car came factory-fitted with a CNG kit whose value is not separately available. For OD cover of the kit under IMT 25 the insurer charges
o: nothing under OD, only Rs 60 under liability
4% on an assumed kit value of Rs 25,000
Rs 60 under OD and 4% under liability
5% extra on the OD premium, and the words limiting liability to the IDV of the kit are deleted
e: IMT 25 note: where the value of the CNG/LPG kit is not separately available, 'premium of Rs...' is replaced by '5% extra on Own Damage premium' and the IDV-limit words are deleted; Rs 60 is separately charged in the liability section.

t: When IMT 26 (fire and/or theft risks only) is attached to a package policy,
o: Section II is deemed cancelled and Section I covers only fire/theft and allied perils while the vehicle is laid up in garage and not in use
both sections continue with a 50% premium reduction
Section I is deemed cancelled and only Section II remains
the policy converts to a Liability Only policy
e: IMT 26 (GR 45A) cancels Section II (liability) and restricts Section I to fire, explosion, self-ignition, lightning, burglary, housebreaking, theft, riot, strike, malicious damage, terrorism, storm, flood and earthquake perils whilst laid up and not in use.

t: For a vehicle insured for fire risk only under GR 45A, which words are deleted from IMT 26?
e: IMT 26 NB (i): for fire risk only delete 'burglary housebreaking theft'; NB (ii): for theft risk only delete 'fire explosion self ignition lightning riot strike malicious damage terrorism storm tempest flood inundation and earthquake perils'.

t: A Liability Only policy with fire and theft cover (GR 45B / IMT 27) cannot be issued for
o: miscellaneous and special type vehicles rateable under Class D
e: IMT 27 is not applicable to Class D vehicles. IMT 26 (fire and/or theft only, without liability) is additionally barred for motor trade Classes E, F and G.

t: A transport operator who has taken IMT 28 (legal liability to paid driver/cleaner) cancels the policy mid-term at his own request. The premium for IMT 28
o: is refunded in full as the cover was never used
is refunded on short period scale
e: IMT 28 (like IMT 38, 39 and 40) provides that in the event of the policy being cancelled at the request of the insured, no refund of the premium paid for the endorsement is allowed; the insured must also keep wage records open to inspection.

t: A company car carries IMT 29 for 4 employees. At the time of an accident 6 employees (including the driver) are on board and two are injured. Under IMT 29 the insured
o: gets full indemnity, as IMT 29 has no number limit
must repay to the insurer a rateable proportion of the amount paid
pays a penalty premium of Rs 50 per extra employee
e: IMT 29 covers employees other than paid driver travelling in or driving the employer's car; if more employees than the number for which premium was paid are carried, the insured repays a rateable proportion of the amount payable.

t: A private car policy is extended to a trailer under IMT 30. Which of the following is correct?
o: The trailer and its contents are covered up to the car's IDV
The trailer need not be identified by registration number
Any number of trailers may be covered under one floater IDV
The term 'trailer' does not include its contents, and persons conveyed by the trailer are not covered except under a contract of employment
e: IMT 30 requires each trailer to be identified by registration number with a separate IDV, excludes contents, and excludes death/injury to persons conveyed by the trailer otherwise than under a contract of employment; floater cover for trailers is prohibited.

t: A two wheeler package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally. During the rally the deductible under Section I is
o: Rs 2,500 or the IMT 22 deductible, whichever is higher
nil, as the rally premium replaces the deductible
e: IMT 31 inserts Rs 5,000 for private cars and Rs 2,500 for two wheelers; for the duration of the event the Section I deductible is this amount or the IMT 22 amount, whichever is higher. Organised racing, pace making and speed testing remain excluded.

t: A defence officer employs a serving soldier as driver of his private car. The liability under service regulations for injury to the soldier can be covered by IMT 32 at
o: a flat additional premium of Rs 100 for a period not exceeding 12 months
e: IMT 32 (accidents to soldiers/sailors/airmen employed as drivers) is granted at a flat Rs 100 irrespective of period not exceeding 12 months; extension beyond 12 months needs further premium. The driver must hold an effective licence.

t: For premium computation the minimum value (IDV) of a private car exceeding 1500 cc is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Minimum IDVs for private cars: not exceeding 1000 cc Rs 15,000; 1000-1500 cc Rs 20,000; exceeding 1500 cc Rs 30,000.

t: IMT 33 (loss of accessories) under a two wheeler policy covers
o: accidental damage to any accessory fitted to the vehicle
theft of accessories only when the vehicle is also stolen
accessories of private cars and two wheelers alike
loss of or damage to declared accessories caused by burglary, housebreaking or theft, at 3% of value subject to a minimum of Rs 50
e: IMT 33 applies to two wheelers only and covers specifically declared accessories against burglary, housebreaking or theft at 3% premium subject to a minimum of Rs 50, overriding the normal exclusion of accessory theft unless the vehicle is stolen.

t: Which of the following is eligible for the Automobile Association membership discount under GR 28?
o: Individuals, joint owners and companies holding valid membership
Individuals and joint owners but not companies
Only vehicles registered in Zone A
e: GR 28: individuals, joint owners and companies who are members of a recognised Automobile Association are eligible for 5% of OD premium (maximum Rs 200 car / Rs 50 two wheeler) using IMT 8.

t: In addition to the 25% OD discount, a certified vintage car is allowed a discount on TP premium of
o: 50%, as directed by IRDA with effect from 1.4.2018
nil - TP premium is never discounted
e: GR 29 gives 25% discount on OD premium to vintage cars certified by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India; a 50% discount on TP premium was additionally allowed from 1.4.2018.

t: A stage carriage bus's permit is temporarily suspended by the State Government for three months and the bus is laid up. The lay-up concession under GR 31
o: is permissible only for the TP portion
is permissible, as suspension of permit by the Government is the exception to the bar on hire-or-reward vehicles
is not permissible for any vehicle used for hire or reward
is permissible only if the bus is less than 5 years old
e: GR 31 bars lay-up concession for trailers, vehicles used for hire or reward and motor trade vehicles, except when permits are temporarily withheld or suspended by the Government.

t: A car owner laid up his car for four months with proper notice. He asks for a cash refund of the lay-up premium. Under GR 31
o: refund is paid only if the lay-up exceeds six months
cash refund is paid on pro-rata basis
cash refund is paid on short period basis
cash refund is not allowed; the amount is adjusted against the next renewal or the policy period is extended, after charging Rs 15 administrative expenses
e: GR 31: pro-rata concession for lay-up of not less than two consecutive months is given by adjustment at next renewal or extension of the policy period - no cash refund - and Rs 15 is charged as administrative expenses.

t: A goods carriage with a private carrier permit is proposed for insurance as a public carrier so that hired goods can be carried. Under GR 34 the office
o: may insure it as a public carrier at 25% loading
cannot insure the vehicle for a purpose other than that permitted by the RTA
may insure it with IMT 42 attached
may insure it as a public carrier if the insured gives an undertaking
e: GR 34 prohibits insuring a vehicle in a name other than the registered owner's or for a purpose other than that permitted by the registering authority.

t: Three months into a two wheeler policy the insured asks to restrict the TPPD limit to Rs 6,000 to save Rs 50. The request
o: may be allowed with IMT 20 from the date of request
may be allowed with pro-rata refund of Rs 37
may be allowed once during the policy under GR 32
must be declined, as the TPPD restriction can be opted only at inception and mid-term change is not permitted
e: GR 39 allows restriction of TPPD cover to the statutory Rs 6,000 only at inception (reduction Rs 200/150/100/50 for CV/taxi/car/two wheeler); mid-term change of TPPD limits is not permitted.

t: A new car with a listed selling price of Rs 12,00,000 is 5 months old at the time of insurance. Its IDV under GR 8 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 8 schedule: not exceeding 6 months - 5% depreciation; Rs 12,00,000 x 95% = Rs 11,40,000.

t: Under GR 43 a private car fitted with a fibre glass fuel tank attracts an additional OD premium of
e: GR 43: all policies covering vehicles with fibre glass fuel tanks attract Rs 50 extra in the OD section, except Class D vehicles where it is Rs 100.

t: A dealer must move brand-new cars 400 km from the manufacturer's plant to his showroom. His Class F road risks policy (radius 80 km) should be supplemented by
o: a Class G internal risks policy
a Motor Trade Road Transit (Class E) policy, one policy for each transit
IMT 41 extending the radius to 400 km at 15% extra
e: For new vehicles the Class F radius is 80 km, extendable only to 120 km at 15% extra; beyond 120 km the dealer needs a Motor Trade Road Transit policy, one for each transit.

t: Under the Internal Risks (Class G) tariff, a dealer who has only a showroom (no workshop) is allowed
e: Class G rating note: dealers having only a show-room get a 50% discount on the premium.

t: For Class E declaration policies the minimum premium for a package cover is
e: Declaration policies under the Road Transit tariff carry minimum premiums of Rs 75 for package, Rs 60 for liability only with fire and/or theft, and Rs 40 for liability only.

t: Under Section II of a Motor Trade Internal Risks policy, which of the following is NOT indemnified?
o: Accidental damage to a customer's vehicle held in trust by the insured
Bodily injury to a visitor caused through a defect in a vehicle
Bodily injury to a member of the insured's family or household
Accidental damage to other property not belonging to the insured, occurring in the premises through the insured's negligence
e: Section II of the Internal Risks policy covers death/injury to persons other than those in the insured's service or members of his family/household, and damage to vehicles held in trust or other property through negligence or vehicle defect, in or about the premises.

t: Under Rule 39 of CMVR, a trade registration mark
o: may be used on up to three vehicles simultaneously
may be used on a customer's registered vehicle under repair
shall not be used on more than one vehicle at a time
may be lent to a sub-dealer in another town
e: Rule 39 prohibits use of the trade registration mark on more than one vehicle at a time, on a vehicle other than that for which issued, or on a vehicle not in bona fide possession of the dealer in the course of business.

t: Which of the following is NOT entitled to apply for a Trade Certificate in Form 16?
o: An individual owner of a fleet of taxis
A financier dealing in hire purchase of vehicles
A person engaged in building bodies on chassis
e: Applicants for trade certificates are manufacturers, dealers, approved repairers, body builders and financiers - the MV Act definition of 'dealer' includes body builders, repairers and those in hypothecation/leasing/hire-purchase business.

t: Which passenger carrying vehicles are rated under Class D of the Commercial Vehicles Tariff?
o: All passenger vehicles with more than 36 seats
e: Among passenger vehicles only ambulances and hearses are rated under Class D; all other passenger carrying vehicles fall under Class C.

t: A cinema publicity van insured with IMT 50 suffers damage to a detachable sound amplifier mounted on it during an accident. The loss to the amplifier is
o: covered as an accessory of the vehicle
not covered, as equipment is covered only if firmly and permanently fixed to the body and not detachable
e: IMT 50 excludes loss or damage to cinematic, photographic or sound equipment, costumes or other technical property on the vehicle unless firmly and permanently fixed to the body and not detachable from time to time.

t: Under a Class E road transit policy for brand new chassis with new tyres, the 50% limitation on tyres can be deleted on payment of
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Deletion of the 50% limitation clause for tyres and tubes under Class E is permitted only for brand new vehicles with brand new tyres on payment of 1% of basic OD premium using IMT 62.

t: A customer falls ill after eating food sold from an insured mobile canteen and sues the owner. Under IMT 51 the insurer is
o: not liable, as illness caused by poisoning or deleterious matter in food or drink supplied from the vehicle is excluded
liable under Section II as a third party claim
liable only if the customer was a passenger
e: IMT 51 (mobile shops/canteens and mobile surgeries/dispensaries) excludes loss to utensils/stock-in-trade (or surgical instruments) and death, injury or illness arising from poisoning, harmful goods or defective treatment supplied from the vehicle.

t: A stage carriage bus has had seats removed to create goods space, reducing its licensed seating capacity by 30%. For rating, the case
o: must be referred to the TAC for special rating as the 20% limit is exceeded
is rated as a goods carrying vehicle under Class A
is rated as a normal bus of similar size under Class C
e: Public passenger vehicles with goods space are rated as a normal bus of similar size under Class C provided the seating capacity is not reduced by more than 20%; beyond that the case is referred to the TAC for special rating.

t: A particular surveyor repeatedly fails to submit reports within 7 days. The office should
o: deduct 10% from his fee for each delayed report
bring the recurrence of delay to the notice of the Regional Office
e: If the surveyor delays he must give a status report with reasons; in case of recurrence of delay by a particular surveyor it should be brought to the Regional Office's notice.

t: Per the OD claim checklist for the insured, repairs to the damaged vehicle should be undertaken
o: immediately, to minimise loss, and bills submitted later
only at the insurer's own workshop
only after the insurer approves the estimate of repairs/replacements
e: The insured's checklist requires intimation to insurers quoting the policy number, submission of a claim form and estimate, and not undertaking repairs till the insurer approves the estimate; a satisfaction certificate is signed after repairs.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a goods carrying vehicle with GVW exceeding 12,000 kg is
e: Goods vehicle minimum IDVs by GVW: up to 2,000 kg Rs 5,000; 2,000-6,000 kg Rs 20,000; 6,000-12,000 kg Rs 30,000; above 12,000 kg Rs 40,000; trailers Rs 3,000 each.

t: Without prior approval of the insurer, a private car owner may authorise accident repairs provided the estimated cost does not exceed
e: The policy permits the insured to authorise repairs up to Rs 500 for private cars and Rs 150 for motor cycles without the insurer's prior consent, subject to intimation and a detailed estimate.

t: Which of the following cities is NOT in Zone A for rating private cars and two wheelers?
e: Zone A for private cars, two wheelers and taxis comprises Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi and Pune; the rest of India is Zone B.

t: On the death of the holder of a goods carriage permit, the person succeeding to possession of the vehicle may use the permit
o: only after fresh permit is granted
for 3 months, provided the RTO is informed within 30 days of the death
e: The MV Act provisions summarised in the material allow the successor to use the permit for three months provided the transport authority is informed within 30 days of the permit holder's death.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: A private car (1000 cc) aged 11 months is damaged. Assessment before depreciation: plastic bumper Rs 9,000, plastic headlamp Rs 7,000, metal bonnet Rs 15,000, painting labour Rs 6,000, paint material Rs 3,000, labour Rs 8,000. The amount payable is
e: Plastic parts 50%: Rs 4,500 + Rs 3,500 = Rs 8,000; metal 5% (6 months to 1 year) = Rs 14,250; paint material 50% = Rs 1,500; painting labour Rs 6,000; labour Rs 8,000; total Rs 37,750 less deductible Rs 1,000 = Rs 36,750.

t: A two wheeler with IDV Rs 55,000 is stolen and not recovered. The claim payable on completion of formalities is
e: Total loss by theft is settled at IDV less the compulsory deductible, which under IMT 22 applies to every event including total loss: Rs 55,000 - Rs 100 = Rs 54,900.

t: A private car (1800 cc) suffers extensive damage assessed at Rs 2,40,000 excluding taxes, not warranting total loss. The surveyor recommends cash loss settlement and the insured agrees. The maximum amount payable is
e: Cash loss settlements require a minimum deduction of 25% of the assessed loss (excluding taxes): Rs 2,40,000 - Rs 60,000 = Rs 1,80,000, less compulsory deductible Rs 2,000 (car above 1500 cc) = Rs 1,78,000; the policy is then cancelled from the date of loss.

t: A 6,000 kg GVW goods vehicle aged 1 year 10 months carries IMT 23. In an accident the vehicle body (metal, Rs 30,000) and two tyres (Rs 16,000) are damaged; labour Rs 5,000. The claim payable is
e: Tyres: 50% depreciation gives Rs 8,000, then the insured bears 50% under IMT 23, leaving Rs 4,000. Metal 10% (1-2 years) = Rs 27,000. Labour Rs 5,000. Total Rs 36,000 less compulsory deductible Rs 500 (GVW not exceeding 7,500 kg) = Rs 35,500.

t: A vehicle aged 3 years 6 months has a current listed selling price of Rs 8,00,000. Its IDV under the GR 8 schedule is
e: GR 8: 3 to 4 years - 40% depreciation; Rs 8,00,000 x 60% = Rs 4,80,000.

t: A car policy with OD premium Rs 10,000 carried 35% NCB (Rs 3,500). Four months into the policy the car is sold to a buyer with no NCB entitlement and the policy is transferred. The NCB to be recovered is
e: GR 17: where the transferee is not entitled to the NCB shown, it is recovered on pro-rata basis for the unexpired period: Rs 3,500 x 8/12 = Rs 2,333.

t: The qualifying examination for an individual insurance agent conducted by the Insurance Institute of India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). IC-38 is the agents' pre-recruitment examination; IC-01/02/11/14 are Licentiate papers.

t: A policy (annual premium Rs 6,000) is extended by 2 months under GR 11 to align the renewal date, pro-rata premium being charged. The insured then does not renew with the same insurer. He must additionally pay
o: Rs 800, the difference between short period premium (30%) and pro-rata premium
e: GR 11: extension for less than 12 months is allowed on pro-rata premium (2/12 x 6,000 = Rs 1,000) provided the policy is renewed with the same insurer; otherwise the insured pays the difference between short period (30% = Rs 1,800) and pro-rata rates = Rs 800.

t: A private car with OD premium Rs 24,000 is fitted with an ARAI-approved anti-theft device certified by an Automobile Association. The discount under GR 30 is
e: GR 30: 2.5% of OD premium subject to a maximum of Rs 500; 2.5% of Rs 24,000 = Rs 600, restricted to Rs 500 (IMT 10).

t: An embassy car imported without customs duty has an OD premium of Rs 20,000 computed on an IDV excluding duty. The OD premium chargeable under GR 37 is
e: GR 37 / IMT 19: where the import duty element is not included in the IDV, the Section I (OD) premium is loaded by 30%: Rs 20,000 x 1.30 = Rs 26,000.

t: A dealer insures six premises in one town under a single Class G policy; the total premium computed for the premises is Rs 40,000. The premium after the multiple-premises discount is
e: Each premises is rated separately and the total may be reduced by 20% for more than 2 up to 5 premises, 25% for more than 5 up to 10, and 30% for more than 10; six premises attract 25%: Rs 40,000 - Rs 10,000 = Rs 30,000.

t: A mobile crane with IDV Rs 80 lakh is to be covered for damage by overturning while in use as a tool of trade. The additional premium under IMT 47 is
e: Package policies for mobile cranes, excavators, drilling rigs and mobile plant may be extended to cover overturning during operational use at 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of Rs 100: 0.5% of Rs 80,00,000 = Rs 40,000.

t: A certified vintage car has a tariff OD premium of Rs 4,000 and TP premium of Rs 3,000. The total premium after vintage car discounts is
e: Vintage cars get 25% off OD (Rs 4,000 - Rs 1,000 = Rs 3,000) and 50% off TP from 1.4.2018 (Rs 3,000 - Rs 1,500 = Rs 1,500): total Rs 4,500.
